jobs.title: Fazeshift | Senior Software Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE (5 days/week) | Full-time | $200k–$235k + equity
jobs.text: I’m Chris, VP Engineering at Fazeshift. We’re nine engineers plus our Founder/CTO and me, and I’m hiring someone who can help us do more, better: increase both what we can build and the quality and sophistication of the software we build. Accounts receivable sounds boring until you look under the hood. It sits at the intersection of money, business relationships, software systems of various vintages, and a huge amount of repetitive human work. Instead of giving finance teams another dashboard to stare at, we’re building AI agents that actually do the work across billing, collections, payments, cash application, and the systems connecting them. We’ve grown revenue 12x since 2024, and eight unicorns now run AR on Fazeshift. A big part of what makes the engineering interesting is that we’re intentionally not the system of record. Our customers already run on ERPs, CRMs, banks, billing systems, payment processors, spreadsheets, and internal software, so we have to understand state across systems we don’t control, act safely in them, and recover when reality disagrees with what an API says should have happened. A timeout doesn’t necessarily mean a write failed. Webhooks can arrive late or twice. A payment may not contain enough information to identify an invoice. In those cases, blindly retrying can be exactly the wrong thing to do. We use coding agents heavily ourselves. Engineers use Conductor, stacked PRs, Linear, and multiple frontier models every day, with internal skills and tooling that let agents drive and validate our local development environment. We’re especially interested in engineers whose development workflow has already materially changed because of coding agents: people who are comfortable delegating meaningful work, keeping independent threads moving in parallel, debugging where agents get stuck, and improving the surrounding system when the workflow breaks down. But generated code is still your code . Judgment, debugging, systems thinking, taste, and understanding what actually shipped matter more here, not less. Our development style is roughly: design enough to find the shape of the problem, then build to learn. There’s a short distance here between noticing a problem, deciding what should happen, building it, and seeing the result in production with our customers. You’ll own meaningful problems from ambiguity through design, implementation, rollout, and production, and you’ll work directly with the people affected by what you build. We’re looking for 5+ years of professional experience, strong TypeScript/full-stack skills, solid systems judgment, and real production ownership. No fintech background needed. Stack: TypeScript/Next.js, tRPC, Prisma/MySQL/PlanetScale, Inngest, AWS. I read every HN application myself. Email chris.zehner@fazeshift.com with HN in the subject, your LinkedIn/GitHub/résumé, and a few sentences about something interesting you’ve built or improved recently.

quantaArticles.author: Perri Thaler

quantaArticles.title: How Do You Take a Picture of a Black Hole?
quantaArticles.description: Astrophysicist Shep Doeleman explains how capturing the first image of a black hole required a telescope the size of the world, and why the next goal is to create a movie.

infoqArticles.title: DoorDash Cuts Grocery Reorder Latency from 16 to 2 Seconds with AI Agents
infoqArticles.description: DoorDash reduced grocery reorder latency from 16 to 2 seconds by precomputing recurring purchase needs using batch LLM inference and deterministic validation. Live catalog resolution keeps product selections current, while an editable shopping interface avoids unnecessary model calls. The company reports that shopping list views doubled and the flow’s order rate increased by approximately 34% By L
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: Netflix Treats GPU Reliability as a Distributed Systems Problem
infoqArticles.description: Netflix has detailed how it is building a reliability platform for large-scale GPU training and inference, using layered health checks, automated remediation, and fault-tolerant training to keep jobs running despite hardware failures. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: The Ladder Is Missing Rungs: Engineering Progression When AI Ate the Middle
infoqArticles.description: Alasdair Allan discusses empirical research from METR and Anthropic on AI coding adoption. He explains the "supervision paradox," where reliance on AI tools disrupts junior skill development, risks institutional context loss, and threatens the long-term engineering pipeline needed to oversee autonomous systems effectively. By Alasdair Allan
infoqArticles.author: Alasdair Allan

infoqArticles.title: Netflix Titus Adds Single-Tenant VM Isolation for Containers
infoqArticles.description: Netflix has added single-tenant Titus, a mode that runs one task alone on its own right-sized EC2 instance. The Compute/Platform team still owns and patches the host, so application teams keep the same API and deployment path By Claudio Masolo
infoqArticles.author: Claudio Masolo

infoqArticles.title: Article: InfoQ AI, ML and Data Engineering Trends Report - 2026
infoqArticles.description: This InfoQ Trends Report offers readers a comprehensive overview of emerging trends and technologies in the areas of AI, ML, and Data Engineering. This report summarizes the InfoQ editorial team’s and external guests' view on the current trends in AI and ML technologies and what to look out for in the next 12 months. By Srini Penchikala, Chip Huyen, Daniel Dominguez, Hien Luu, Arthur Casals
infoqArticles.author: Srini Penchikala, Chip Huyen, Daniel Dominguez, Hien Luu, Arthur Casals

infoqArticles.title: Podcast: AI, ML, and Data Engineering InfoQ Trends Report 2026
infoqArticles.description: In this episode, members of the InfoQ AI and ML editorial staff and friends of InfoQ discuss the current trends in the domain of AI, ML and Data Engineering. One of the regular features of InfoQ are the trends reports, which each focus on a different aspect of software dev. These reports provide the InfoQ readers and listeners with a high-level overview of the topics to pay attention to this year.
infoqArticles.author: Chip Huyen, Daniel Dominguez, Hien Luu, Arthur Casals

infoqArticles.title: Microsoft Retires Azure Deployment Environments with No Replacement Product
infoqArticles.description: Azure Deployment Environments retires on February 22, 2027 and Microsoft names no successor, telling teams to use Bicep or ARM templates directly. Microsoft Dev Box follows on September 18, 2028, pointed at Windows 365, which Microsoft says is not a one-to-one replacement. Remaining Dev Box workloads should expect deletion. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Google Adopts DPoP to Strengthen OAuth 2.0 Against Token Theft and Replay Attacks
infoqArticles.description: Google's OAuth Platform has recently introduces support for Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP), an OAuth 2.0 security mechanism designed to mitigate token theft and replay attacks. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Bug0 Releases QA Agent to Automate Regression Testing With Cached Playwright Replays
infoqArticles.description: QA Agent is a new source-available Playwright library for agentic browser regression testing. The agent associates test instructions expressed in natural language to actions on the user interface, caches those when appropriate for faster CI replays, remapping them to test specifications when the user interface changes. Verification is based on multi-model consensus and vision model evaluations. By
infoqArticles.author: Bruno Couriol

infoqArticles.title: How to Make Artificial Intelligence More Environmentally Sustainable
infoqArticles.description: IT is responsible for about 2 - 4% of all global emissions, and electricity use at Microsoft and Google has climbed because of AI, according to their own reports. Sustainability ought to be a top-level architectural concern. Some recommendations are: use pre-built and smaller models, run compute where low-carbon electricity is abundant, and train on renewable energy. By Ben Linders
infoqArticles.author: Ben Linders

infoqArticles.title: QCon AI New York 2026 Program Committee Picks: Agent Identity, Context Costs, and Open-Source Infere
infoqArticles.description: Who authorizes an agent’s actions, and how should teams manage growing context costs? The QCon AI New York 2026 program committee shares six session picks that tackle these questions, alongside open-source inference, agent standards, and audio AI. By Artenisa Chatziou
infoqArticles.author: Artenisa Chatziou

infoqArticles.title: Anthropic Says Nobody Needs a Mental Model of Claude Code. Practitioners Are Testing That
infoqArticles.description: Anthropic has published how the Claude Code team reviews code now that Claude writes roughly 90% of it, including a claim that nobody keeps a complete mental model of the codebase. The post documents a pull request that ran more than fifty review rounds overnight, a reviewer spending most of its effort on pre-existing code, and a control the team says it does not yet have. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Datadog Builds a Specialist AI Model for SRE Investigations
infoqArticles.description: Datadog has released Scout, a model trained to investigate production problems. It runs inside Bits Investigation, the company's AI SRE product, where it can pick up an alert, look through telemetry and suggest what caused the problem. Datadog engineers and a small number of customers are using it in a closed preview. By Matt Saunders
infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Introduces Web Search API for AI Applications
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare has recently launched a beta Web Search API through AI Gateway. Available through REST APIs and Cloudflare Workers, it provides unified logging, access controls, and billing, and supports bring-your-own-provider keys. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: Airbnb Cuts Recommendation Staleness from 2 Days to Seconds with Chronon
infoqArticles.description: Airbnb extended its Chronon feature platform with Push Mode and Near Real-Time Model Transform to update sequence-based recommendation embeddings within seconds. The architecture reduced embedding staleness from nearly two days to under a minute and improved offline NDCG by 1.67%, while online testing increased uncancelled bookings by approximately one-third of a percent. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili
